title: In 1958, the US Accidentally Dropped a Nuclear Bomb on South Carolina

scenes.text: In 1958, the US dropped a nuclear bomb on South Carolina. By accident.
A crewman climbed into the bomb bay to fix a loose pin. He hit the release by mistake.
The bomb fell 15,000 feet into a family's garden.
Two tons of explosives went off. The crater was 70 feet wide and 35 feet deep. The house collapsed.
The nuclear core was still on the plane. Six people were hurt. Nobody died.
The family got 54,000 dollars. The crater is still in the woods today.

description:
On March 11, 1958, a US Air Force B-47 accidentally dropped a Mark 6 nuclear bomb on Mars Bluff, South Carolina, after a crew member unhooked it while trying to fix a locking pin.
The bomb's two tons of conventional explosives detonated, leaving a crater about 70 feet wide and 35 feet deep and collapsing a family home; six people were injured. The nuclear core was stored separately on the aircraft, so there was no nuclear blast.
What is the biggest accident you have ever heard of that somehow hurt nobody?
thumbnail_text: A NUKE FELL ON A GARDEN
first_comment: The family sued the Air Force and settled for 54,000 dollars, about 600,000 today. Was that enough for a nuclear bomb in the garden?
